Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for Pakistan's second innings. Bangladesh are seen in a huddle near the ropes before striding out to the centre. It will be the left-hand right-hand combination of Saim Ayub and Abdullah Shafique to open the innings for Pakistan. Taskin Ahmed has the red cherry in hand and he is raring to go. Off we go...
... THIRD INNINGS ...

Right then, it’s even Stevens in the Test, with around 20 minutes of play remaining in the day. Pakistan will be hoping to get through this period unscathed, while Bangladesh will be looking to put the openers, who have been fielding all day, under pressure and take a wicket or two before the close of play. Back in a bit for Pakistan's reply.

An excellent recovery from Bangladesh! Who would have thought they would reach 262 after they were reeling at 26/6 in the morning, conceding a lead of only 12 runs? Initially, it was the pair of Litton Das and Mehidy Hasan who added up 165 runs for the 7th wicket. Mehidy got out on 78 and Litton batted on along with the tail. He found an able alley in Hasan Mahmud who did his bit at the other end with Litton trying to face as many balls as he could. Litton continued his impressive innings after bringing up his 4th Test century, and it even seemed like Bangladesh might erase the entire deficit. However, with an eye on resting the pacers ahead of the second new ball, Agha Salman was introduced and he ended up quickly wrapping up the innings.

OUT! LBW! Pakistan close out the Bangladesh innings with a narrow lead of 12 runs! An appeal for LBW and the finger is raised! Nahid Rana sends it upstairs! Floats the ball up on the off stump and gets it to turn just a little bit. Rana doesn't offer any shot to it, wearing it straight on the front pad in front of the stumps. The Ball Tracking shows the ball to be clipping the leg stump and it is umpire's call. The on-field decision is upheld. Bangladesh are bundled out for 262 runs.

OUT! CAUGHT! Saim Ayub grabs a very well-judged catch to end a brilliant innings from the lone warrior of Bangladesh, Litton Das! Agha Salman fires the ball into the pitch as he sees Litton Das stepping down the track for a big shot. Litton Das gets this one off the the toe end, a rare sight in this innings from him and it goes flat and low to the right of long on. Saim Ayub at long on makes a good sprint to his right and dives, grabbing the ball with both hands inches above the ground. A much-needed breakthrough for Pakistan. End of a marathon innings from Litton Das as he falls for 138 with Bangladesh trailing by 12 runs.

Khurram Shahzad, who had an expensive first spell after Lunch, returned with a short-ball strategy, but it didn't go as planned for Pakistan as Litton Das and Mehidy Hasan handled it with ease. However, against the run of play, Shahzad struck twice, dismissing Mehidy Hasan and Taskin Ahmed in successive overs. Through their 165-run stand, Mehidy and Litton set a record for the highest partnership for the seventh wicket after the first six wickets had fallen for under 30 runs. Bangaladesh's hopes now rest on Litton Das to reduce the deficit, which currently stands at 81. Khurram Shahzad, in particular, will be riding high on confidence and will look to add to his tally of 6 wickets to wrap things up quickly after Tea. Join us back at 10.15 am GMT for the start of the final session.

SESSION SUMMARY -  27.3 overs, 118 runs and 2 wickets. Pakistan will head into the break feeling a lot better after a strong end to the session. For most of the session, it was one-way traffic, with Bangladesh in control, but Pakistan managed to pull things back just before the interval. Earlier, Litton Das made his intentions clear right after Lunch, quickly dispatching any loose deliveries. Pakistan's bowlers, who were disciplined in the morning session, faltered in the early half of the second session. Together with Mehidy Hasan, he helped his side avoid the follow on. After reaching their respective fifties, the two batters put their head down and continued on their merry way.

Mehidy Hasan and Litton Das walk out to resume their innings. Khurram Shahzad will start the proceedings with the ball for Pakistan. Let's play...
... DAY 3, SESSION 2 ...

With the first day's play lost, the follow-on deficit has now been reduced to 150 instead of 200. This means Bangladesh need to reach 125 to avoid the follow-on. We’ve witnessed a remarkable turn of events, and if the first session is anything to go by, we’re in for an engrossing couple of sessions ahead. Do join us back for the start of the second session at 7.40 am GMT.

For Bangladesh, with the new ball just two overs old, the first hour was always going to be challenging, and they struggled to meet the challenge. Their batting faltered with a mix of poor shot selection and some exceptional pace bowling contributing to their downfall. Reeling at 26/6, Mehidy Hasan and Litton Das got together and brought some much-needed stability and calmness to the visiting dressing room. Mehidy Hasan, in particular, did not shy away from playing his shots. As the ball lost its shine, the shot-making became easier for him. Abrar Ahmed was introduced into the attack, but his efforts did not bring Pakistan any success.

Wow, who could have predicted this? It’s been a session that belonged entirely to Pakistan. They have dismantled the Bangladesh lineup, picking up 6 wickets in just 24 overs and conceding only 65 runs. The duo of Khurram Shahzad and Mir Hamza were nothing short of sensational, using the movement in the air and off the pitch to their advantage. Shahzad set the stage with his incisive bowling, and Hamza followed suit, leaving Bangladesh struggling. Both bowlers made a consistent effort to keep the stumps in play and were duly rewarded for their efforts.
Floats the ball fuller on the off stump line and Litton Das gets back in the crease again and blocks the ball down to end the first session of play on Day 3. Bangladesh walk off at 75/6.

Commentary.Commentary: Drinks break! Pakistan have been outstanding so far on Day 3. They have pushed Bangladesh back and have picked up 6 wickets in the session, giving away just 26 runs in the first 11 overs. Since the entire first day's play was lost due to rain, the follow-on deficit has been reduced to 150 instead of 200. Importantly, it has been given on-field, so, the ball just has to clip the stumps for the decision to be upheld. Khurram Shahzad bowls it on a length from around the wicket, shaping back in, on middle and leg, Shakib Al Hasan's head falls over to the off side as he tries to get across and clip it off his pads. There is nothing on UltraEdge and the Ball Tracking shows the ball to be clipping the leg stump. The on-field decision will stand and Bangladesh slip further in trouble. Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for the action to commence on Day 3. The sun is shining in all its glory as the two umpires make their way out to the middle. Pakistan are in a huddle near the ropes before taking their respective positions in the field. They are followed by the two Bangladeshi openers, Shadman Islam and Zakir Hasan. Mir Hamza will kickstart proceedings with the red cherry for Pakistan. Three slips and a gully in place. Away we go...

Mehidy Hasan is in for a chat. He says he's very happy with his contribution with the ball. He admits he was initially a little concerned about the greenish-looking surface but felt more confident as the game progressed. Mehidy adds that while he didn't get much turn in the first session, the pitch began to offer more assistance from the second session onward. He shares that his primary focus is always on keeping things tight and drying up the runs. Feels that if they bat well, they have a good chance of taking the lead.

PITCH REPORT - Bazid Khan is pitchside, inspecting the deck ahead of the start of Day 3. He notes that the ball bounced more on Day 2 - technically the first day of this Test, compared to the opening day of the first Test. This wicket reminds him of the old-time surfaces in Rawalpindi and Karachi. He points out that this surface is much harder and quicker than the one used in the first Test. While there's a nice grass covering, Bazid highlights a few bare patches around the short-of-a-length area, suggesting that bowlers who hit those spots could extract more purchase and some indifferent bounce. He adds that while the ball is new, bowlers should pitch it up to search for swing, and once the movement stops, they should switch to bowling into the wicket.

Heading into Day 3, all eyes will be on the Bangladeshi openers, who survived a tricky 2-over period late on Day 2, where Shadman Islam was dropped first ball. Although the pitch eased out to some extent as the day progressed yesterday, there continued to be some assistance for the bowlers, particularly spinners, which will pose a challenge for Bangladesh's lineup. Bangladesh will be focused on starting well and putting Pakistan under further pressure. Stay tuned for an exciting day of cricket, starting early with the first ball at 4.45 am GMT.

For Pakistan, skipper Shan Masood initially led the charge with an intent-laden fifty. His inning, however, was cut short, preventing him from making a more significant impact. Saim Ayub, too, could not kick on after reaching his fifty. Agha Salman, showing tenacity, held the fort with the tail, managing to push the total past 250. His efforts were crucial in preventing a complete collapse and ensuring Pakistan had a respectable total.

Bangladesh's bowlers shone brightly on a surface that offered assistance, particularly for the spinners. Mehidy Hasan emerged as the star of the day, claiming a five-wicket haul and dismantling Pakistan's batting lineup. Pakistan, batting first, could only muster 274 runs, with only three of their top seven batters converting starts into fifties. Despite the familiar conditions, the Pakistani batters struggled to impose themselves against a determined Bangladeshi bowling attack.

Hello and a warm welcome, folks! As Day 3 dawns in Rawalpindi at the ongoing Test match between Pakistan and Bangladesh, the visitors have their noses in front after an impressive performance on Day 2. Bangladesh have shown remarkable resilience and skill on this tour of Pakistan, and they continued their dominance on a day marked by disciplined bowling to inflict setbacks on the hosts.
... DAY 3, SESSION 1 ...

Right then, after the first day dampened our spirits with no play possible, the second day delivered and how! The momentum swung back and forth, but at the end of the day, Bangladesh will be the happier of the two sides. With Pakistan trailing in the series, they need to force a result with three days left in the Test. Moreover, with rain expected on the last two days, they will need to strike early on Day 3 and make the most of the new ball and early movement on offer. As for Bangladesh, there are runs to be had if the batters apply themselves. We saw that batting became easier as the ball got older. It will be yet another early start with the first ball on Day 3 to be bowled at 4.45 am GMT. As always, you can join us earlier for the build-up. See you then. Cheers!

Earlier in the day, after Pakistan were inserted into bat, Taskin Ahmed executed a perfect setup to dismiss Abdullah Shafique in the first over. Shan Masood came out with intent, and together with Saim Ayub, they successfully weathered the early storm. Masood, in particular, focused on rotating the strike with singles and twos to keep the scoreboard ticking. Despite the early setback, this partnership helped Pakistan recover and head to Lunch at 99/1.

After the early wicket in the first over of the first session, Pakistan dominated the rest of that period. Bangladesh needed to find a way back into the game, and they did just that by chipping away at the wickets throughout the second session. The momentum shifted with Mehidy Hasan's twin strikes, and the rest of the bowlers supported him by maintaining tight control. Saud Shakeel, who was dropped on 1, couldn't make the most of his reprieve, and things got even better for Bangladesh when Shakib Al Hasan trapped Babar Azam right in front of the stumps just before the Tea break.

As play resumed after Tea, Nahid Rana cranked up the pressure and was duly rewarded when he dismissed Mohammad Rizwan. This breakthrough opened one end for Bangladesh, putting Agha Salman and Pakistan in a tough spot. However, the situation brought out the best in Salman, who smartly farmed the strike and mixed caution with aggression to keep the scoreboard ticking. Dropped before he had even opened his account, Salman made the most of that error by Zakir Hasan. His knock of 54 added some respectability to the Pakistan total, but given they were 107/1 in the second session, they will be disappointed to have ended with just 274.

Wow, an eventful couple of overs to end the day's play! Pakistan will be left wondering what might have been if Saud Shakeel had held on to that catch off the very first ball. Who knows, they might have even snatched another wicket before Stumps. While the first session belonged to Pakistan, Bangladesh roared back in the next couple of sessions. As many as four catches went down, and had they been taken, could have put Bangladesh in an even stronger position at the close of play.
